column2: did I really get that fat?”
“That's not what I meant!
...Although, well, you have put on weight, it's true.”
{n2} took off her goggles too and showed me a smile.
Seeing that smile for the first time in hours was like the sun peeking out from behind the clouds.
I looked at {n2} again.
Her long black hair stood out beautifully against the white ski wear.
Gliding down any tough slope with ease, she had been the center of attention on the slopes.
I think everyone must have expected a beautiful face beneath those goggles.
That's how ski resorts are.
With {n2},
I thought.
With {n2}, no one would be disappointed.
I'd been fed up all afternoon with {n2}, a snow-country native, rubbing in the difference in our skills, but right now I felt proud.
I knew not only her face, but also how attractive the figure hidden under that thick ski wear was.
“One more run. Shall we?”
“Whaaat?
You still want to ski?”
I asked back, worn out.
“Don't say that, come on,
okay?{r}{p}Just one more.
Just one, okay?”
{n2} gave me her best smile and pressed her hands together.
I'm weak to that smile.
“Fine.
Just one more.”
I agreed reluctantly.
Maybe I'd improved a little: I fell less and made it down before sunset.
“All right, time to head back.”
We got into the 4WD we'd borrowed from Mr. Kobayashi.
I'd met {n2} this April at the university.
Through bold and persistent attacks, I'd managed to get as far as having dates with her, and that was this autumn.
No matter how hard I pushed there was never any response, and it even felt like I was wrestling alone, so honestly I was surprised when she was the one to invite me to go skiing together.
Her uncle and aunt run an inn in Shinshu {C3}(now Nagano){C0}, she said.
It's a bit far from the ski resort and inconvenient, so even in season it apparently has few guests, and they'd let us stay for a bargain price.
Of course I gladly said yes, and yesterday,{@}
December 21st, we arrived here in Shinshu.
By the time we got back to the inn, it was completely dark and snow had started falling.
The Kobayashis' inn was called “Spur,” a name that seemed made to appeal to ski tourists.
A stylish white-based inn with a log-cabin look, apparently magazines had even featured it and it was getting popular.
That “bargain price because it's slow” was something Mr. Kobayashi said so that {n2} and I wouldn't feel indebted; I realized that after arriving.
Unfortunately, or rather naturally, {n2} and I had separate rooms.
We went back to our rooms to change, then met in the lounge{@}
beside the first-floor entrance.
On the sofas set around a large table, some guests were relaxing until dinner began.
“Well, well, you two lovebirds.
Looks like ya got yer fill of skiing.”
Mr. Kayama said sarcastically when he saw my utterly exhausted face.
He's the president of a company in Osaka and apparently an old friend of Mr. Kobayashi.
A middle-aged man, with laugh lines and a shiny bald head that stood out.
Before I could reply, {n2} cut in.
“I wanted to ski a bit more, actually.”
She gave me a sidelong glance.
I shrugged, but said nothing in particular.
Beside Mr. Kayama sat his wife.
She looked no more than thirty-something, but I didn't know her real age.
Her name was Haruko.
And that Mrs. Haruko said to me with a coquettish laugh:
“These days it seems the girls have more energy, don't they?”
Exactly right.
I nodded inwardly, looking at the trio of office ladies who seemed to have arrived today.
“Oh, noooo!
Kana, stop it!”
They had spread out what looked like a guidebook and were giggling, talking about something we couldn't hear.
The girl in the middle, thin with long hair, was marking the magazine with a red pen.
She was the one called Kana.
Was it a restaurant they had their eye on, or something?
The one on the right was called Keiko.
A cute, slightly plump girl with short{@}
hair.
The one on the left, with big glasses,{@}
seemed to be named Aki.
“Which one's your type?”
{n2} whispered in a cold voice.
“Which one's your type?”
{n2} whispered in a cold voice.
“Uh, no...
well...”
“That's not it!
I wasn't looking with that in mind...”
Just as I was about to make excuses, the cuckoo clock on the wall struck seven.
“You're the only one I see,
“Is that so?”
“It's true!
Look into my eyes.
...See,
only {n2} is reflected in them, right?”
“...Silly.
How embarrassing, in a place like this...”
Then I noticed a PlayStation sitting in a corner of the lounge.
Then I noticed a PlayStation sitting in a corner of the lounge.
Holding back my urge to play, I gazed at {n2}.
Just as I was forgetting my surroundings and sinking into a world of just the two of us, the cuckoo clock on the wall struck seven.
“Dinner is ready.
Please come to the dining room.”
Mr. Kobayashi appeared as if he'd been waiting for the cuckoo.
It would normally be too early for dinner, but thanks to the hard exercise I realized I was famished.
I had to muster all my self-control to keep from running.
“Oh, a PlayStation!”
I forgot all about {n2} and ran over to it.
“Hey, {n1}!
...Honestly!”
{n2} cried out in exasperation, though she was smiling.
“Was it here from the start?
Weird...
Oh well. Let's see... what games are there?...
'Otogirisou' and 'Kamaitachi no Yoru'?{r}{p}Hmm...
Both look fun.
Which one should I try?”
I fell into thought, looking at the game packages.
“Okay,
let's go with 'Otogirisou'!”
I took the DISC out of its case, set it in the PlayStation, and switched it on.
“It looks kind of scary.”
{n2} said, peering over from behind.
“Kyaa, scary!”
{n2} flicked the switch off.
“Hey, hey.
What are you doing?{r}{p}Nothing's even started yet.”
“...Sorry.
Please, pick a different one.”
“...Fine.
Then let's play 'Kamaitachi no Yoru' instead.{r}{p}...This one looks scary too, but...
don't turn it off this time.{r}{p}If it's scary, just don't look.”
“Okay.
I'm fine.”
I swapped the software for 'Kamaitachi no Yoru' and switched it on again.
“I knew it'd be 'Kamaitachi no Yoru'!”
“No way,
it looks scary...”
{n2} said, selfishly.
“If it's scary, go over there.”
“Aw, how cold.
Fine,
I'll put up with it.”
I set the DISC and switched on the PlayStation.
“It says to enter names.
What should I do?”
“Why not just put in our names?”
“Good idea...
{n2}, there.”
When I entered the names and pressed the confirm button, the screen changed to a ski slope...

made it to the rest house at the foot of the mountain
and caught my breath

kicking up a cloud of snow.

and I couldn't see a thing.
“Ha ha,
{n1}, you look just like a snow
man.”
I heard {n2} laughing.
I took off my goggles and
brushed the snow off my body.
“I'm exhausted.{r}{p}Let's call it a day
here.”
“You're so weak.
...Oh well, that's
fine.
So, shall we head back?”
“Somehow this is just like us.”
{n2} murmured.
“...Yeah.
It is.”
As I kept playing, a strange feeling gradually came over me.
By the time we got back to the inn, it was completely dark and snow had started falling.
“Spur,” run by the Kobayashis, had a log-cabin look outside and was a stylish inn with a white-based interior.
We went back to our rooms to change, then met in the lounge beside the entrance.
Sofas were set around a big brown table.
We decided to sit there and wait until dinner began.

Beer...
no, bring us whiskey!”

I am Noyol Kaamai.”
I got drunk for the first time in ages and made a big racket too.
